title: Base components
description: Every component is shown with all its states side by side: rest, hover, keyboard focus, active, disabled, loading. That is the only way to check that a disabled state stays readable and that a working button does not change width.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.note: A page carries only ONE primary button. The secondary frames it, the ghost serves toolbars, the link form is only for an action that must sit inside a sentence. “Danger” is reserved for what destroys or refuses — never for “save”. Clicking “Save” below triggers a real loading state.

badges.title: Badges
badges.note: Five intents, not one more, each matching a kind of information. A grey badge is not a design failure: it is the ordinary case. The solid version is reserved for what must be visible from across the room.
badges.dotNote: The three coloured badges carry a THEME from the database. Its colour is entered in the back office and nothing guarantees its contrast: it is therefore rendered as a dot, never as a text background. The label keeps the theme tokens and stays readable in both light and dark.

status.title: State badges, theme tags, counters
status.note: The STATE badge does not look like the information badge: square, uppercase, preceded by a dot. That distinct shape is deliberate — in a dense programme the eye must separate at a glance what describes an activity from what says where it stands. Two colours are not obvious: “in progress” is YELLOW, because an activity under way calls for attention and is not a success; “postponed” is PURPLE, because a postponement has already been arbitrated and asks for nothing — confusing it with a warning drowns out what still needs handling.
status.themeNote: Three theme tags at most, the rest fold away. The edition holds {total} in the database: past three on a card they stop informing — the reader retains “this activity is about everything”. Hidden themes remain announced to screen readers.
status.counterNote: The accent tone is reserved for what awaits action; neutral is the default.

chips.title: Filter chips
chips.note: A badge informs, a chip acts: it states which filter is applied and how to remove it. The first two carry a theme from the database, the next two a translated enumeration value — both kinds of label live side by side, and that is exactly the trap not to fall into.
chips.fixedNote: The “Event” chip has no cross: it materialises the administration scope, which cannot be removed. An imposed filter must stay visible without suggesting it can be dropped.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.note: Three signals for one piece of information: a distinctly shaped icon, a colour, a title. An alert recognisable by colour alone is lost on a colour-blind reader and invisible in print. RESULT alerts are announced as soon as they appear; context alerts interrupt nothing.

info.title: The call for proposals closes in three days
info.body: The deadline is 30 June 2027 at 23:59, Belém time. Draft proposals are not forwarded to the committee.

success.title: Proposal submitted
success.body: Proposal COP31-00147 has been forwarded to the selection committee. A receipt has been sent to the contact address.

warning.title: Two reviews missing
warning.body: This proposal has received 2 of the 4 expected reviews. No decision can be settled until the count is met.

danger.title: The requested slot overlaps a scheduled session
danger.body: The pavilion has a single stand: two activities cannot be held there at the same time. The overlap is not blocked — the team arbitrates — but it must be resolved before the programme is published.

alerts.compact: Fields marked with an asterisk are required.

cards.title: Cards
cards.note: Hierarchy comes from the rule and the whitespace, not from shadow. The link wraps the TITLE rather than the whole card: a fully linked card makes text impossible to select and produces an unwieldy accessible name. The click target, however, does cover the whole card.
cards.body: A two-hour workshop bringing together national focal points from six countries around financing mechanisms.
cards.selected: The selected state serves the slot planner and comparison screens.
cards.sunken: The sunken card carries supporting content: a rule reminder, contextual help, a summary of the active filter.
